Both did the job — I marked "Making Sense of Color Palettes," hit "Read later" above the collection, and it showed up next to the Kyoto one with 2 results. The behavior you assumed is exactly what I want: I can turn it on, the card visibly shows it's flagged, there's a dedicated spot to see just those, and search still works.

Between the two, the checkbox version feels the most natural to me. A little tick box labeled "Read later" makes it obvious I can turn it on and just as easily turn it back off — it reads as a switch I control. The button that flips to "Saved for later" was fine too, but the checkbox makes the on/off nature clearer at a glance. So let's go with the checkbox.

One thing I want to confirm, since it's the whole point of a "read later" pile for me: once I've actually read something, I want to un-flag it so it drops out of that Read later list and my pile shrinks as I get through it. That un-marking is easy with this checkbox, right? Assuming so, this works for me.
